frequency_scope: Only Kim2014 ground-state symmetric stretch and bend replace Table V values. Unobserved antisymmetric stretch stays 1034 cm^-1. Zero-point energy is excluded: all partition energies are relative to v=0, keeping D0 fixed during the thermal calculation.
electronic_scope: Three doublet electronic origins from Kim2014; all three states are assigned identical rotational and vibrational partition factors. Added factor is Q_el/2 because Table IV already contains ground weight 2. This factorization is a limited diagnostic, not a complete state-specific partition sum.
limitations: Table I contains published equilibrium estimates after ion fragmentation, multiple-ionization, cross-section and multiplier-gain corrections; the underlying ion-intensity readings and full calibration covariance are unavailable. No raw instrument reprocessing is claimed.

Unweighted second-law fits reproduce the printed reaction 1 and 2 slopes and standard errors. Reaction 3 does not reproduce the printed 82.0 +/- 2.9 kJ/mol; original fit weighting, grouping, unrounded observations or printing differences remain unresolved. No data points are removed or changed.

Table I prints reaction 2 average temperature as 1046 K although its observations span 1913-2186 K; the separately calculated harmonic mean is about 2046 K. The original value is retained, not silently corrected.

At 2087 K Table I prints lnK2=5.51 and H0(2)=-74.8 kJ/mol. They do not close in the present third-law replay; both were visually rechecked and retained. No inferred correction is treated as an observation.

Original Table IV is used for VO2. Current official JANAF V/VO thermal tables are used on the H0 reference; the exact historical 1975 JANAF printed pages have not been independently compared. JANAF formation enthalpies and logKf are not used as modern energy anchors.

Table IV does not explicitly state its pressure convention. Separate 1 bar and 1 atm assumptions are retained. Every reaction has Delta nu=0, so a common standard-pressure conversion cancels; mixing a 1 atm VO2 table with 1 bar V/VO tables does not. Experimental pressures quoted in atm do not by themselves establish the Table IV convention.

Complete reaction 1 and 3 third-law re-reductions remain unavailable without the original Eu/EuO thermal functions. Their selected historical VO2 energies share EuO and VO references and must not be pooled as independent measurements.

The modern VO anchor is Merriles2020 D0=6.545(2) eV to V(4F3/2)+O(3P2), retained in current curated spectroscopy provenance. Its uncertainty is a conservative assigned limit, not stated as one sigma; no new combined VO2 uncertainty is assigned.

The partial thermal change leaves geometry, rotation, antisymmetric stretch, anharmonicity, higher electronic states and state-specific rovibrational functions unresolved. The old bent geometry and old antisymmetric frequency are held, not revalidated.

Applying the same partial thermal model to the second-law reduction moves inferred H0 by +delta H(VO2), while the third-law reduction moves by +delta G(VO2). Their combined-model results differ by about 21 kJ/mol. This failure of method agreement prevents interpreting the approximately 1175 kJ/mol third-law endpoint as a validated new D0; original equilibrium calibration and a complete thermal model require further evaluation.
No selected rounded H0 is refitted as an observation, no covariance-free pooling is performed, and no newly recommended D0 or curated update follows from this partial re-reduction.
